ei.title: Computing the sum or average of several positive and negative values indeed...
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: Computing the sum or average of several positive and negative values indeed lies within the normal repertoire of what elementary circuits of neurons can do without consciousness. Even a monkey can learn to make a decision based on the total value brought about by a series of arbitrary shapes, and the firing of parietal neurons keeps track of the sum. In my laboratory, we proved that approximate addition is within grasp of the human unconscious. In one experiment, we flashed a series of five arrows and asked subjects whether more arrows were pointing right or pointing left. When the arrows were made invisible by masking, participants were asked to guess, and indeed they thought that they were responding randomly, but in reality they continued to do much better than chance would predict. Signals from their parietal cortex gave evidence that their brain was unconsciously computing the approximate sum of the overall evidence. The arrows were subjectively invisible, but they still made their way into the brain's weighting and decision systems.

✅ ① lies: 'Computing ~ lies within ~'에서 주어(Computing)에 호응하는 3인칭 단수 동사로 올바른 어법

det.korean: ④ uncertainty(불확실성) → evidence(증거)
det.analysis:
✅ ① average(평균): 합이나 '평균'을 계산한다는 문맥에 적절

det.korean: ③ exceptional(예외적인) → normal(정상적인)
det.analysis:
✅ ① firing(발화): 두정엽 뉴런의 '발화'라는 문맥에 적절

det.tip: 'within the normal repertoire'에서 normal은 기초 신경 회로가 의식 없이도 할 수 있는 '일반적인' 능력 범위를 뜻합니다.

questions.passage: Computing the sum or average of several positive and negative values indeed lies within the normal repertoire of what elementary circuits of neurons can do without consciousness. Even a monkey can learn to make a decision based on the total value brought about by a series of arbitrary shapes, and the firing of parietal neurons keeps track of the sum. In my laboratory, we proved that approximate addition is within grasp of the human unconscious. In one experiment, we flashed a series of five arrows and asked subjects whether more arrows were pointing right or pointing left. When the arrows were made invisible by masking, participants were asked to guess, and indeed they thought that they were responding randomly, but in reality they continued to do much better than chance would predict. Signals from their parietal cortex gave evidence that their brain was unconsciously computing the approximate sum of the overall evidence.
